**This is a pre-release for testing.** It is not marked Latest and is not intended for general use. If you want a stable build, use [v0.4.8](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/releases/tag/v0.4.8).

This is the first beta of the 0.5.0 line. The rebuilt world is now the **published v2 scenery library**, which this build reads by default, so there is no staging URL to set. The package manager gains a **Settings tab**, and the log, signal and startup problems the alpha builds listed are fixed.

| Platform | Download |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 (glibc 2.34 or newer) | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-beta.1-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS, Apple Silicon | `xearthlayer-v0.5.0-beta.1-arm64-macos.tar.gz`, or Homebrew (below) |

No `.deb`, `.rpm` or AUR package is built for previews. There is no Intel Mac build; Intel Mac users can build from source. The `xearthlayer-publish` tarballs are the package publishing tool, which testers do not need.

---

## Setup

Close X-Plane and stop any running XEarthLayer before you start.

### 1. Install the binary

**Linux:**

```bash
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-beta.1-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-beta.1
```

**macOS:** install [macFUSE](https://macfuse.io) first, including the one-time approval of its system extension. [docs/macos.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.0/docs/macos.md) walks through it.

With Homebrew, the pre-release channel follows every alpha, beta and rc build, and `brew upgrade` keeps it current:

```bash
brew install --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-beta.1
```

If macFUSE is already installed from its own installer, add `--skip-cask-deps`. Already on the channel from alpha.2? `brew upgrade --cask xearthlayer/tap/xearthlayer@prerelease` is all you need.

From the tarball instead: Safari unpacks the download into a folder for you. With Safari:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads/xearthlayer-v0.5.0-beta.1-arm64-macos
```

With any other browser:

```bash
cd ~/Downloads
tar xzf xearthlayer-v0.5.0-beta.1-arm64-macos.tar.gz
```

Then:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
mv xearthlayer ~/.local/bin/
xearthlayer --version        # should print 0.5.0-beta.1
```

The binary is signed and notarized. The first run needs a network connection, because macOS checks the notarization once. If `xearthlayer` is not found, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to your shell profile and open a new terminal.

### 2. Coming from alpha.1 or alpha.2?

Your configuration and packages carry over. The packages you installed from the staging library are the same releases the v2 library publishes, so there is nothing to reinstall. Bring the configuration up to date:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

It points `packages.library_url` at the v2 library (XEarthLayer already reads the v2 library in its place before you run this), and it removes `prefetch.mode` (see What changed). Then go to step 4, or straight to step 5 if you already have the regions you fly.

### 3. Coming from v0.4.8, or new to XEarthLayer?

New to XEarthLayer on this machine? Run `xearthlayer setup`. When it finishes it offers to open the package manager, which takes you to step 4.

Coming from v0.4.8: the first command you run copies your `config.ini` to the platform's standard location (`~/.config/xearthlayer/` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/XEarthLayer/` on macOS) and may ask you to confirm. Accepting is safe: nothing else is moved, and the old `config.ini` is kept, so v0.4.8 still works if you go back to it. The copy reads the v2 library, and the message says so; the old file keeps the library v0.4.8 can use. Then:

```bash
xearthlayer config upgrade
```

The rebuilt world replaces the old one, and the two must not be installed together. Remove every old package **before installing anything new**:

```bash
xearthlayer packages remove --all --force
xearthlayer packages remove --all --type overlay --force
xearthlayer packages list    # should report no packages installed
```

If you had no overlays, the second line prints `Error: Package manager error: No overlay packages are installed`, which is harmless. There is nothing to clean up by hand in `Custom Scenery`: XEarthLayer rebuilds its entries there every time it starts.

To have each ortho install bring its region's overlays, which is off by default:

```bash
xearthlayer config set packages.auto_install_overlays true
```

You can also change it on the package manager's Settings tab.

### 4. Install the regions you fly

Open the package manager:

```bash
xearthlayer packages
```

Press `2` for the Library, move with the arrow keys, mark regions with `Space`, press `i` and confirm with `y`. Press `3` to watch the downloads and installs. `?` lists every key, and `q` quits. [docs/package-management.md](https://github.com/samsoir/xearthlayer/blob/develop/0.5.0/docs/package-management.md) describes it in full.

The command line works as before, and takes several regions at once: `xearthlayer packages install na-canada eu-west`. A region code, or the start of one, installs every package beneath it.

| Region | Covers | Download |
|---|---|---|
| `NA-USA-BERMUDA-BAHAMAS` | Contiguous US, Alaska, Hawaii, Bermuda, the Bahamas, Turks and Caicos | 14.1 GB |
| `NA-MEXICO-CENTRAL` | Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean | 4.5 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-WEST` | Canada west of 95° W | 10.2 GB |
| `NA-CANADA-EAST` | Canada east of 95° W | 13.2 GB |
| `NA-GREENLAND` | Greenland | 0.8 GB |
| `SA-WEST` | Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile, the Guianas | 9.2 GB |
| `SA-EAST` | Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, the Falklands | 8.8 GB |
| `EU-WEST` | Europe west of Russia, Iceland, Scandinavia, the Mediterranean | 16.1 GB |
| `EU-EAST` | European Russia west of the Urals | 3.7 GB |
| `AF-NORTH` | North and West Africa | 7.3 GB |
| `AF-SOUTH` | Central, East and Southern Africa | 9.1 GB |
| `AS-INDIA-MIDDLE-EAST-HIMALAYAN` | Middle East, Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent | 16.8 GB |
| `AS-CHINA-MONGOLIA` | China and Mongolia | 18.5 GB |
| `AS-ASIA-PACIFIC` | Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia, the Philippines | 11.6 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-CENTRAL` | Siberia from the Urals to Lake Baikal | 4.8 GB |
| `AS-RUSSIA-EAST` | The Russian Far East | 6.4 GB |
| `OC-AUSTRALIA-NZ-PACIFIC` | Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands | 5.5 GB |

Sizes are download sizes. The whole world is about 161 GB. Antarctica is not available yet.

### 5. Run

```bash
xearthlayer run
```

---

## What changed since alpha.2

- **The v2 scenery library.** The rebuilt world is published as library generation v2, at `https://xearthlayer.app/packages/v2/xearthlayer_package_library.txt`, and this build reads it by default. The library v0.4.8 reads stays as it was, so older builds keep working. A configuration naming the old library or the alpha staging library reads v2 straight away.
- **A Settings tab in the package manager.** Press `4` for the `[packages]` settings, with the help for each. Enter edits and Enter again saves; Esc cancels. The tab is read-only while `xearthlayer run` is active or a job is queued or running.
- **Each command keeps its own log.** Only `xearthlayer run` writes `xearthlayer.log`, emptied when it starts. The package manager and the `packages` commands add to `xearthlayer-packages.log` beside it, and every other command writes no log. Opening the package manager during a flight no longer empties the flight's log.
- **`xearthlayer run` stops cleanly on SIGTERM and SIGHUP,** as it does on Ctrl+C, including when its terminal is closed.
- **A faster start.** `run` no longer measures every installed package before the dashboard opens, which could take minutes with the whole world installed, and the scenery index builds from file names: about 17 seconds for the whole world on a warm disk, where it took over four minutes.
- **The X-World Pro scenery order prompt is visible,** and answering it once is remembered until `scenery_packs.ini` changes. Startup warnings are counted on the dashboard's Status pane, since the dashboard replaces the screen they were printed on.
- **Package sizes are recorded at install.** The package manager no longer re-reads every file of every package after each install or delete. A package installed by an earlier build is measured once, the first time its size is shown.
- **`prefetch.mode` is gone.** Prefetch is on or off by `prefetch.enabled`, which stays `true` by default. A configuration that had `mode = disabled` still has prefetch off: it is read as `enabled = false`, and `config upgrade` writes it so.

---

## What we most want tested

### 1. Moving to the v2 library

Whether you came from an alpha or from v0.4.8: does `xearthlayer packages` list the 17 regions, does `xearthlayer config get packages.library_url` show the v2 URL after `config upgrade`, and do installed packages show as up to date rather than as updates or unknown packages?

### 2. The package manager and its Settings tab

Installing several regions at once, deleting one, refreshing with `r`, and quitting with `q` while jobs are running (it asks first, cancels cleanly, and a second `q` leaves at once). On the Settings tab: change a setting, check `config.ini` has the new value, and try an invalid one (it is refused with the reason). Anything that looks stuck, any row that never finishes, and any key that does not do what `?` says.

You can install new packages while `xearthlayer run` is active; they are used the next time `run` starts. Updating or deleting is refused while `run` is active, with a banner saying so.

### 3. Start up and shut down

How long `xearthlayer run` takes from the command to the dashboard with your packages installed, and whether closing the terminal or `kill` (SIGTERM) leaves the mount cleanly, so the next `run` starts without complaint.

### 4. Carried over from the alphas

No pauses or purple tiles at DSF boundary crossings (prefetch stands aside while X-Plane waits), night lighting over cities, the rebuilt scenery, SimHeaven X-World Pro with `packages.xworld_pro` on, and on macOS a Gatekeeper that accepts the binary with no prompt.

### The dashboard

The Status pane leads its lines with emoji. If your terminal shows empty boxes instead, `xearthlayer config set tui.symbols plain` uses plain marks. The default, `auto`, tries to detect this for you.

---

## How to report

The flight log is `xearthlayer.log`, and the package manager's log is `xearthlayer-packages.log`, both at `~/.local/state/xearthlayer/` on Linux and in `~/Library/Logs/XEarthLayer/` on macOS unless you changed `logging.file`. `xearthlayer run` empties the flight log when it starts, so copy it before the next flight. Then run:

```bash
xearthlayer --version
xearthlayer diagnostics
```

The most useful report is your route, aircraft and flight time, the last few `Prefetch sample` lines from the flight log, and what looked wrong. For a package manager or install problem, say what you pressed and what the screen showed, and attach `xearthlayer-packages.log`.

---

## Known issues, please don't report these

**FUSE read counts on the dashboard are low on macOS.** macOS serves repeat reads of a texture from its own cache, so XEarthLayer only sees the first one. Nothing else depends on that count.

**Saving a setting rewrites `config.ini` from its template.** Comments you added to the file by hand are lost, as they are with `xearthlayer config set`. The values are kept.

**Antarctica is not in the library yet.**
